proposals: GIZ should publish a post-completion results report for MiCacao measured against its own logframe targets — 2,688 male and 672 female farmers applying the tool, 1,008 and 252 reaching a 10% premium — so that a project that closed in April 2025 is judged on results, not on targets.

BMZ should require every project funded through the i4Ag Fund to publish end-of-project indicator results on a public page within a fixed period after closing, so that the target-versus-result gap this post found for MiCacao cannot recur silently across the fund’s portfolio.

The European Commission should publish a monthly count of EUDR due-diligence statements submitted for cocoa, by origin country, in the run-up to 30 December 2026, so that readiness for a twice-delayed deadline is measured before it arrives rather than after.

The European Commission should issue technical guidance stating what a farm-level cocoa origin record must contain and whether offline-captured data synced later is acceptable, since this post finds the hard part has always been getting physical-world data onto any platform, not the ledger itself.
